case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Ashok Dixit and Another
respondent:
Ashok Dixit and Another
Supreme Court of India

16 February 2000
Criminal Appeal Nos. 238-39 of 1989
The Judgment was delivered by : S. N. Phukan, J.
1.  This appeal by the State is directed against the judgment and order dated 16.08.1988 passed by the High Court of Allahabad in Criminal Appeal Nos. 2742, 2743 and 2338 of 1984 arising out of Sessions Trial No. 202 of 1982. The learned Additional Sessions Judge, Agra in the above Sessions Case convicted accused respondents - Ashok Dixit and Chaman Lal under Sections 302 and 307 IPC and Section 25 of the Arms Act and sentenced them accordingly. Two separate appeals were filed before the High Court by the respondents-accused and one appeal by the State for enhancement of the sentence. The High Court dismissed the appeal filed by the State and allowed the appeals filed by the respondents-accused and acquitted them of their charges.

facts: The appeal was filed by the State against the judgment and order passed by the High Court of Allahabad in Criminal Appeal Nos. 2742, 2743 and 2338 of 1984 arising out of Sessions Trial No. 202 of 1982.
On August 8, 1982, at around 9:00 p.m., a sound of gunshots was heard coming from the house of Dr. Dubey, his brother Bhagat Dayal Dubey and their family members were present in the house.
The police officers Vijai Bahadur Singh and Uma Shanker Yadav took position behind the varendah of the house and P.W.1 along with his two sons stood near the grill of the western varendah.

At that time, they saw accused Brijendra Kumar tumbling down the staircase to the ground floor followed by present two accused respondents Ashok and Chaman Lal, and three accused were apprehended by the two police officers.
issues: Whether the identification of the accused by PW-2 is reliable?
Whether the evidence of a child witness must be evaluated carefully as a child may be swayed by what others tell him and as an easy prey to tutoring?
Whether the prosecution has failed to establish the occurrence beyond reasonable doubt?
petitioner_arguments: The State argued that the identification of the accused by PW-2 is reliable.
The State argued that the evidence of a child witness must be evaluated carefully as a child may be swayed by what others tell him and as an easy prey to tutoring.
The State argued that the prosecution has failed to establish the occurrence beyond reasonable doubt.
respondent_arguments: The accused respondents argued that the identification of the accused by PW-2 is unreliable.
The accused respondents argued that the evidence of a child witness must be evaluated carefully as a child may be swayed by what others tell him and as an easy prey to tutoring.
The accused respondents argued that the prosecution has failed to establish the occurrence beyond reasonable doubt.
court_reasoning: The Court held that there was no identification by PW-2 of accused-Ashok.
The Court held that the evidence of a child witness must find adequate corroboration before it is relied on.
The Court held that the prosecution has failed to establish the occurrence beyond reasonable doubt.
holding: The appeal was allowed and the judgment and order passed by the High Court of Allahabad in Criminal Appeal Nos. 2742, 2743 and 2338 of 1984 arising out of Sessions Trial No. 202 of 1982 were set aside.
